title: Why did my actual tolls cost disappear from the P&L after entering port expenses?
text: When a port with port function I (Canal transit) is selected in estimates, the estimated port expenses of this port will automatically fall under Tolls instead of Port Expenses in the P&L. Upon fixing the estimate, the Tolls cost in the actual P&L will initially follow the estimated Tolls cost. When actual port expenses are entered, the associated ledger code(s) determine if the expense falls under Tolls or Port Expenses. If all port expenses are recorded using a ledger code that is not a Tolls expense type, the port expenses will be recorded in the Port Expenses section and the previously estimated Tolls cost will be automatically removed.

title: Why did Voyage Status change from Completed to Closed?
text: The Voyage Status will not change unless a user has manually done this, either one-by-one or through the bulk closing option within the Voyage List, which requires the Close a Voyage Module Right. To determine why this occurred: Look at the IMOS Audit Trail or IMOS - Audit Trail Report, filter by Voyage and Vessel. Add Last Modified On and Last Modified By columns to the Voyage List. Check the Voyage Manager Revisions panel. You cannot bulk update in reverse (i.e., change all Closed voyages to Completed); you must do that manually.

title: Why does an additional "uninvoiced" line appear under Emission costs in Voyage PnL?
text: [image] It has been noticed that sometimes, in the Voyage PnL, under Emission costs, an additional line appears, which is indicated as "uninvoiced" and doesn't match with the actual emission invoice. This is happening because the emission invoice doesn't cover the whole period of the voyage. That is why this extra line appears in the PnL, which covers the remaining period. In order to remove this extra line in the PnL, the duration of the Allowance Invoice needs to be amended to match the duration of the voyage. [image][image]

title: Why does Company Code in Voyage Manager differ from the Vessel Properties?
text: When you create a Vessel and link it with an internal company in the Vessel Properties, the Company Code usually flows and updates the associated TC contracts and fixtures. However, when the Company Code in the Vessel Properties is different from what you see in the Voyage Manager, the following reasons may apply: Creating a Voyage from a Fixture - the Company Code from the Estimate flows into the Fixture and then to the Voyage. Creating a Voyage from TC Contract instead of a Fixture - the Company Code specified in the TC contract will be used to update the Company Code in the Voyage.

title: Why does my manual Demurrage/Despatch Calculation differ from the Laytime Calculation menu?
text: Discrepancies between manual demurrage/despatch calculations and the system's Laytime Calculation menu results usually stem from the way demurrage and despatch hours are displayed. If the HH:MM Format is enabled, the system presents time in hours and minutes rather than in days or decimal hours. Displayed hours are also rounded to the second decimal place. The demurrage amount calculation always relies on the Balance Days value when the HH:MM Format checkbox is disabled. Calculation based on days: Demurrage Amount = Balance Days x Demurrage Rate per Day. Calculation based on hours: Demurrage Amount = Decimal Hours x Daily Demurrage Rate / 24.

title: Why does my voyage fail to synchronize?
text: The following error is primarily based on information that does not match or contradicts information entered on a consecutive voyage. It is important to compare information in port activities from one voyage to another. [image] The common result of the error is overlapping commencement and completion times between consecutive voyages. Changing these times and saving will resolve the error and allow the closing of the voyage.

title: Why doesn't "Opr Qty" reflect on the Bunker invoice, when we have multiple liftings?
text: There are some occasions when multiple liftings exist for a port, however on the bunker invoice the Opr qty is not visible for both liftings. [image] The above behavior is due to the bunkering forms/report for the two fuels are sent/created separately so they are not able to link to one Bunker Purchase. IMOS doesn't support the ability to invoice bunkers stemmed on multiple Activity Reports on a single bunker invoice. To rectify that, both liftings need to be included in one report.

title: Why does the data in a report or IMOS list not match what is found in the Voyage?
text: When comparing values shown in an IMOS List against the values visible inside the Voyage Manager P&L, users may notice discrepancies. This is expected behavior and is not a data error. The key reason is that all lists in IMOS display data from the current snapshot, whereas the Voyage Manager P&L shows live, real-time calculated values. The 'current' snapshot gets updated every time that the voyage is saved.

title: Why does voyage bunker consumption not appear in the Voyage P&L?
text: When you have valid bunker consumption and are not seeing the bunkers being reported as an Expense in your Voyage P&L, one of the following scenarios is possible: Bunker inventory price is zero because no price entered for lifting or initial bunkers on latest or previous voyages. Business Rules are missing: VBNK - VCXXX (*XXX = Fuel type code). Mapped chart of accounts for the above Business Rules are not of Expense type.

title: Why do Transit Ports have their Port Sequence numbers change when adding or removing a port from the itinerary?
text: When adding a port within a block of Transit Ports on an itinerary, all ports within the block will have an increase in Port Sequence Number. The change in Port Sequence No. is because transit ports (canals and passing points) are auto-inserted by the distance calculation. To preserve port sequence numbers, select "Lock Transit Port" from the port options dropdown. [image][image][image]

title: Why is a vessel's newly added fuel type not appearing in Voyage Bunkers?
text: If a new fuel type is added to a vessel, that fuel type will not appear on existing or previously created voyages. To ensure the new fuel type is present in the voyage: Uncommence the voyage by setting status to Scheduled > Delete the Voyage > Open the existing estimate > Click the hyperlink for the Vessel > Open Vessel Details > Save the vessel > You will be presented with a prompt to synchronize vessel details with the Estimate; click Yes. Then reschedule the voyage.

title: Why is bunker consumption in the Voyage P&L different from the linked Estimate?
text: You may encounter situations where the bunker consumption in the Voyage P&L may differ from its linked Estimate. Possible reasons: The Estimate Was Created after the Voyage - To resolve: Save the Estimate and confirm. FIFO Queue Is Not Enabled in the Estimate - Enable configuration flag CFGEnableVoyestInitBunkerQueue. When enabled, Estimates allow multiple initial lots for each bunker type. The Estimate calculates the bunker cost per FIFO rule.

title: Why is Cargo deleted when removed from a voyage itinerary?
text: If a cargo contract is created in Voyage Manager (or Voyage Fixture), the default system behavior is to delete those cargoes from the system when they're removed from the voyage. CFGPreserveGeneratedCargoes controls this behavior. If users want to preserve any freight contracts created in Voyage Manager, they should enable this flag.

title: Why is Demurrage or Despatch not showing on the Actual P&L Column?
text: When the question of why Demurrage/Despatch not showing on P&L (Actual Column) arises, review the Laytime Status. The 3rd Column of the table header states "Default Value of Include In Voyage P&L check box". The corresponding Laytime Calculation Status determines if the P&L check box is ticked. Users have the choice to select a Laytime Calculation Status. If the status has Default Value of "Cleared", the check box will not be ticked. If "Selected", the check box will be ticked.

title: Why is my IMOS list exporting as an empty Excel file, even though the list isn't empty?
text: This issue usually occurs when there are one or more filters applied to the list that do not have any values set (i.e., blank filters). These empty filters unintentionally exclude all data during export. Solution: Check your filters, remove or update empty filters, then try exporting again.

title: Why is the despatch/demurrage invoice status in the Transaction Summary showing 'Posted' even though the invoice has not been posted?
text: If demurrage is allocated to other counterparties in the Demurrage Allocation Summary, the despatch/demurrage invoice status in the Transaction Summary will automatically be reflected as Posted even though the invoice is not yet posted. If you are not intending to use this demurrage allocation function, you may remove the demurrage cost allocation via: Reject the initial Demurrage Cost Allocation invoice, click on the Allocation function in the Laytime Calculation, delete all cost allocations entries.

title: Why is the discharge port(s) in the operations itinerary not appearing in my CP Terms Details?
text: It is a common occurrence for vessels to have multiple loading and discharging ports in their itinerary. Users may overlook filling in the Cargo column in the Voyage itinerary table for each port. To ensure all loading/discharging ports are accurately reflected: Navigate to the Itinerary table and click on the 'Cargo tab'. Locate the port with missing cargo information. Select the appropriate cargo grade from the dropdown options. Provide the necessary details as per your CP Terms. Save the changes.

title: Why is there a discrepancy between the cargo booking screen and the database?
text: It is expected that when you are reporting on the Cargo Booking, it's displaying the last-saved values from the Cargo Booking, but you can update any lifting in that booking independently, and updating the lifting does not automatically update the booking. The database is going to show the value from the last time the booking was viewed and saved.

title: Why is voyage bunker consumption different from Vessel details?
text: By default, the Voyage Manager prioritizes using the bunker consumption information from the Performance tab of the linked Head Fixture or Time Charter In over the figures specified on the Vessel Consumption tab. When configuration flag CFGExcludeTcConsFromBunkerCalcs is enabled, the Voyage Manager will reference the bunker consumption information specified in the Vessel Consumption Tab instead.

title: Why only one freight rate is applied to different cargo grades in freight invoice?
text: Scenario: User has created a cargo contract which includes different cargo grades with different pricing (freight rates), belonging to the same counterparty. All cargo grades are loaded and discharged in the same ports. Upon raising a freight invoice, they all display the same freight rate. Solution: For having different freight rates, it would be recommended to create separate cargo contracts, so that the correct freight rate is picked up for each cargo grade.

title: Will the total port days at an M-port change after importing a cargo that is loaded/discharged at this port?
text: No, the original total port days at the M-port will be preserved. The number of extra port days (XPD) at the port will be automatically adjusted by the system after the relevant cargoes are imported, so that the sum of port days (as imported via the CP terms of the cargoes) and XPDs, will still equal the original total port days at the M-port before the cargo import.
